current_recheck.methodSummary: Contre-revue qualitative limitée aux 10 constats explicitement consignés dans le rapport initial, sans modification des fichiers de cours ou de code. Le manifeste de formation (entrée 24) désigne un seul JSON courant : client/public/data/courses/building_ai_agents_with_haystack__01.json, courseId building_ai_agents_with_haystack__01. Les données actuelles ont été rapprochées constat par constat du rendu réel de LessonViewer.tsx, de la progression chapterProgress.ts, du registre blockRegistry.ts, du thème learningDesign.ts, ainsi que des composants effectivement impliqués ChapterQuiz.tsx et ProjectorPlayer.tsx. Le manifeste p0-p2-remediation-manifest.json ne contient aucune entrée pour ce courseId : aucun retrait n’est donc documenté. L’index courant a bien été mis à jour pour annoncer 5 écrans, 5 vidéos et 0 activité (trainingIndex.json:6783-6795), mais cette correction de compteur ne constitue ni la restauration des 6 TP attendus par datacampImport.expected, ni une trace de retrait documenté ; les promesses/transitions pratiques persistent. Aucune absence d’écran n’a été assimilée à une correction. Tous les constats sont tranchables par les données et le code de rendu actuels, donc aucun n’est classé externally_unverifiable. Score : les cinq scores de chapitre du rapport initial (64, 56, 61, 64, 60) sont conservés faute de résolution démontrée des constats qui les pénalisent ; moyenne non pondérée = 305 / 5 = 61,0/100. Le score n’infère ni disponibilité réseau/qualité audiovisuelle réelle ni réussite d’une session apprenant authentifiée.

I’m Bilge from deepset, and I’ll be your instructor for this course. In this course, you’ll learn how to build smart AI agents using Haystack. Whether you're new to agents or just new to Haystack, you're in the right place.

You won’t just be learning about agents in theory. You’ll actually build one step by step with real components, tools, and data. And this won’t be a generic agent either. You’ll create a healthcare agent that can respond to user queries by combining up-to-date online information with private, structured patient data.

Your agent will be able to access the web to fetch current medical insights — like treatment guidelines or drug interactions and query an SQL database that holds patient records: things like age, conditions, and prescribed medications.

We’ll be using Haystack to build our agent. Haystack is an open-source AI orchestration framework — built for AI engineers, data scientists, and Python developers. It gives us the tools to build real-world, compound, agentic systems that can reason, retrieve, act, and respond like autonomous agents, multi-modal apps, or scalable RAG systems. Haystack is designed to be modular and model-agnostic — meaning we can build our system with our choice of LLMs and tools, without being locked into one provider or platform.

6. Haystack avec des outils
Additionally, in this course, we’ll be using OpenAI as our LLM provider and to let the agent search the web, we’ll connect it to the Google Search API through Serper.

7. Notre démarche de construction
By the end of this course, you’ll not only understand how agents work, but you’ll also have a working prototype that can interpret natural language queries, make smart decisions, and act on them using the right tools at the right time.

8. Passons à la pratique !
Let’s get started. In the next exercise, we’ll start exploring Haystack components by talking to a language model directly. Understanding how to communicate with LLMs is the first step toward building a complete agent.

Get ready to customize, connect, and boost your Haystack pipeline!

Préparez-vous à personnaliser, connecter et booster votre pipeline Haystack !

projectorSlides.title: Bilan et prochaines étapes
projectorSlides.script: Congrats on making it to the end of this course!
projectorSlides.instructorTitle: DevRel Engineer for Haystack at deepset

projectorSlides.title: Vous avez créé un agent réel avec Haystack !
projectorSlides.script: You’ve just completed a hands-on journey into building AI agents using Haystack. You’ve learned how to create systems that don’t just generate responses but reason, interact with external data sources, and make decisions.

projectorSlides.title: Agents capables de raisonner et d’agir
projectorSlides.script: At the beginning, we interacted directly with a language model. It could generate text, but it had no awareness of the world or tools to act with.

projectorSlides.title: Agents capables de raisonner et d’agir
projectorSlides.script:
Then, we built our first agent by giving it access to tools, starting with real-time web search, and later, structured patient records in an SQL database. 
Along the way, we learned how to use Haystack to build an AI agent in just couple of steps.

projectorSlides.title: Agents capables de raisonner et d’agir
projectorSlides.script: First, we integrated the SerperDevWebSearch component as the agent’s first tool, giving it access to real-time web information. We then improved the agent’s transparency and traceability through custom configurations.

projectorSlides.title: Agents capables de raisonner et d’agir
projectorSlides.script: Next, we built a text-to-SQL pipeline that converted natural language questions into SQL queries, executed them on a patient database, and returned the results. Finally, we wrapped that pipeline as a tool and connected it back to the agent. That’s how we combined dynamic reasoning with structured workflows, all within a unified system.

projectorSlides.title: Prochaines étapes
projectorSlides.script:
If you want to explore further, you can level up by building multi-agent systems, adding multimodal capabilities like image or PDF support, and deploying your agents in production with Hayhooks.
Agents are one of the most exciting frontiers in AI, and you now have the skills to help shape what comes next.

projectorSlides.title: Passons à la pratique !
projectorSlides.script: Thanks for joining me on this journey, happy building!
